text:
Predicates:
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
In(x, y) ::: x is in y.
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Donated(x) ::: x has been donated.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
HasMineInRange(x, y) ::: range x has a mine.
InTexas(x) ::: x is in Texas.
InNewMexico(x) ::: x is in New Mexico.
No(x, y) ::: x has no y.
HasMine(x) ::: x has a mine.
RangeIn(y, z) ::: range y is in z.
RangeHasMine(y) ::: range y has a mine.

Premises:
MountainRange(picuris) ∨ MountainRange(texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are in New Mexico or Texas.
In(juan, picuris) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
LocatedIn(harding, picuris) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine is located in the Picuris Mountains.
Donated(harding) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine was donated.
∃x (Mine(x) ∧ Donated(x)) ::: There exists a mine that was donated.
∀x (RangeIn(x, texas) ∧ HasMine(x) → No(x, y) ∧ HasMineInRange(y, texas)) ::: No mountain range in Texas that has mines has been donated.

Conclusion:
InNewMexico(juan) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.
